---
title: "How to Run a Heuristic Evaluation of a Website"
description: "Find usability problems in an existing site before you redesign it."
---

A heuristic evaluation is a quick way to find usability problems by reviewing a website against a set of established design principles. It is a good first step in a redesign because it needs no participants and can be done in a few hours.

This article uses the redesign of Flame Kabob, a Persian restaurant website in Las Vegas, as an example.

## Before you start

You need:

- The website you want to review
- A list of heuristics. Most teams use [Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/).
- A spreadsheet to record problems

## Steps

1. List the key tasks. Write down the few things users most need to do on the site. For a restaurant, this is usually viewing the menu, checking hours and location, and placing an order.
2. Walk through each task. Complete each task yourself and note every point where you hesitate, get lost, or make a mistake.
3. Match each problem to a heuristic. Record which principle the problem breaks. This keeps your findings objective and easy to explain to others.
4. Rate the severity. Use a scale from 0 (not a problem) to 4 (prevents users from finishing a task), so the team knows what to fix first.
5. Summarize the findings. Group similar problems and list the most severe ones at the top.

![The original Flame Kabob homepage, with inconsistent fonts and colors and unclear navigation icons.](images/flame-kabob-original.png)

## Example findings

The Flame Kabob evaluation found these problems:

| Problem | Heuristic broken |
|---|---|
| Homepage styles were visually inconsistent | Consistency and standards |
| The menu was not interactive | Flexibility and efficiency of use |
| Navigation icons were poorly prioritized | Aesthetic and minimalist design |
| Colors and fonts did not match the brand | Aesthetic and minimalist design |

## Tips

- Have two or three people evaluate separately, then combine the lists. One evaluator usually misses many problems.
- A heuristic evaluation does not replace real users. Follow it with interviews or usability testing, as the Flame Kabob team did with 12 user interviews.
